fr:ul.fr:li: functions U : A .ob → X .ob and F : X .ob → A .ob
a family of isomorphisms (π_{x,a} : A(F(x), a) ≅ X(X, U(a)))_{a ∈ A, x ∈ X}

fr:mainmatter.fr:p: An adjunction core extends to an adjuction iff ∀a,b ∈ A. ∀x ∈ X. I commutes, and iff ∀x,y ∈ X. a ∈ A. II commutes. The adjunction is unique when it exists.
The original theorem is stated in terms of \mathcal {V}-enriched categories, but we only treat the simple case of Homset-categories here.

fr:mainmatter.fr:p: We use the same notation and definitions of η, ϵ, \overline {F}, \overline {U} as the explicit proof of the precursor lemma. The definition of \overline {F}, \overline {U} in the short proof presupposes that U is a functor, so we're scrupulous to avoid circularity.
This proof is rather low tech and is lifted straight from the paper. It's also how you'd attack the precursor head-on. The utility is that it holds in enriched categories.

The forward directions are trivial. Suppose (F, U, (π_{a, x})_{a ∈ A, x ∈ X}) extends to \overline {F} ⊣_π \overline {U}. Then I expresses that ∀g : A(a, b). ∀f : A(F(x), a). π_{x, b}(g∘f) = \overline {U}(g)∘π_{a, x}(f). This is exactly the condition that ∀g : A(a, b). π is natural in a at g, which is certainly true of an adjunction. II expresses something similar (dual).
The nontrivial directions are the backward directions.

fr:li.fr:p: (I) wts I ⟹ \overline {U} is a functor. Suppose ∀a,b ∈ A. ∀x ∈ X. I holds. Then in particular, ∀c ∈ A. I holds at x = U(c).

fr:li.fr:p: Combined with the earlier proof that \overline {U}(1ₐ) = 1_{\overline {U}(a)} (which just follows by definition), we've shown that \overline {U} defines a functorial action on morphisms. Actually, we saw earlier that I expresses that π is natural in a, so we've met the preconditions of the precursor lemma, thus there is a unique extension \overline {F} st \overline {F} ⊣_π \overline {U}.
There's two ways ways to see the uniqueness situation:

fr:ul.fr:li: (Going backwards) Since the definitions of \overline {F} and \overline {U} (in the precursor) are not dependent on the other functor, the total adjunction \overline {F} ⊣ \overline {U} is the unique one extending the core by applying the uniqueness result of the precusor to each functor in turn, just knowing the other is a well-defined functor.

fr:li.fr:p: (II) wts II ⟹ \overline {F} is a functor. This is dual.

fr:mainmatter.fr:p: (For V-enriched categories, ) If V is thin, all diagrams commute, thus an adjunction core always determines an adjunction.
Set isn't thin, but 2 is, thus for posets, an adjunction core gives rise to a thin adjunction, as remarked here. I don't know how useful this lemma is for ordinary Homset categories.
